name: The Hatter

gender_note.quote: He had been looking at Alice for some time with great curiosity

base_age_note.reason: Not stated; a working tradesman in his prime, worn down early ('I’m a poor man').

hair.style: thick, shaggy and uncombed, sticking out in tufts below the hat brim; untrimmed sideburns
hair.reason: Not described; unkempt to match his poverty and agitation.

eyes.shape: large and prominent, often stretched very wide
eyes.quote: The Hatter opened his eyes very wide on hearing this
eyes.reason: Wide eyes sourced; colour designed for an unsettling pale stare.

skin.quote: staring at the Hatter, who turned pale and fidgeted

face.default_expression: restless, rude, over-excited at the tea-table; trembling and fidgeting in the witness box
face.quote: he kept shifting from one foot to the other / the Hatter began, in a trembling voice
face.reason: Fidgeting and trembling sourced; the tremor is the realistic period reading of a hatter's mercury poisoning; face structure designed.

build.body_type: tall, thin and gangly, all elbows and knees
build.scale_reference: about 1.35x Alice's true size (135 cm); with the hat he towers over the tea-table
build.reason: Not stated; a tall, spindly silhouette under a tall hat.

marks.description: an oversized tall hat that is stock-in-trade, not his own, with a paper price-ticket still tucked in the band ('In this style 10/6')
marks.quote: “It isn’t mine,” said the Hatter. / “I keep them to sell,”

marks.description: a pocket-watch he shakes and holds to his ear; at the trial a teacup and a piece of bread-and-butter

default_outfit_tone.summary: a worn, too-short frock coat in faded bottle green, loud yellow-and-brown checked trousers, a large floppy cravat tied in a loose bow, a stained waistcoat, the tall price-ticketed hat
default_outfit_tone.silhouette_1862: an 1862 tradesman's Sunday best gone shabby: long thin legs, short sleeves showing bony wrists, dominated by the tall hat
default_outfit_tone.quote: I’m a poor man, your Majesty
default_outfit_tone.reason: Poverty sourced; colours and cut designed. Costume detail by 06-art/costume.

touches: no animal coding; character-coded by the price-ticketed hat, tremor and fidgeting
performer_coding.limits: no cartoon make-up or wild wig colours; keep it a real, shabby 1862 tradesman

prompt_base_en: a tall, thin, gangly English hatter of about thirty-five in 1862, shaggy uncombed dark-brown hair under an oversized tall hat with a paper price ticket '10/6' in the band, large pale grey staring eyes, long pallid narrow face, shabby faded green frock coat, loud checked trousers, loose floppy cravat
